title: Vital-Rate Feedback and Threshold Harvesting in Size-Structured Populations
summary: Size-selective harvesting is often justified by the intuition that larger individuals have higher value and should therefore be harvested above a critical size. We study a controlled size-structured transport model in which a scalar environmental variable, generated by the population itself, modifies the vital rates \(g(E,l)\) and \(μ(E,l)\). The first result is a corrected stationary closure theory: crowding-suppressed growth increases residence density at the inflow, so the closure derivative is not determined by pointwise profile monotonicity.
